overall: The AG found the Belmont Math Working Group was a subcommittee of the School Committee subject to the Open Meeting Law, that it violated the law including by inadequate May 31 minutes, and that the Committee itself did not violate the law; the working group having disbanded, the only order was to amend those minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the math working group was a subcommittee of the School Committee; the Committee argued it fell within the Connelly exception as a superintendent-created advisory group.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, the Working Group was specifically created to make recommendations to the Committee, thus clearly meeting the definition of “subcommittee.”

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the working group failed to post timely notice, held meetings not open to the public, deliberated outside posted meetings, and failed to keep adequate minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Working Group was a subcommittee of the Committee and that it failed to comply with the Open Meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the working group's May 31 meeting minutes were inadequate because they did not summarize the discussions held.
allegations.key_passage: We find the May 31 meeting minutes to be insufficient where they note that discussions on various topics were held but do not summarize those discussions.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the School Committee itself violated the Open Meeting Law through the working group's formation and conduct.

remedy: Co-chairs to amend the May 31 meeting minutes to the best of their ability, using any means available, and certify compliance to the AG within 60 days; if unable, explain the efforts in writing within 60 days.
remedy_passage: we order the co-chairs, Principal Koza and Math Director Golden to amend the minutes of the May 31 meeting, to the best of their ability, using any means available, including notes, records, and the recollections of those in attendance at the meeting.
